title: General Quantum-Relativistic Field Theory: Unified Theory of Gravity and Black Hole Universe Formation
content: This paper offers a novel perspective on gravity by conceptualizing it as a quantum fluid and exploring its potential integration with a theory positing black holes as catalysts for the formation of new universes. By synthesizing principles from general relativity, quantum mechanics, and thermodynamics, we hypothesize that gravity at the smallest scales behaves as a Bose-Einstein condensate. Utilizing the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for quantum fluids in conjunction with Einstein's field equations, we propose an effective field theory that aims to bridge classical and quantum descriptions of gravity. This unified theory seeks to provide new insights into gravitational singularities, the quantum structure of spacetime, and the role of black holes in cosmic evolution. Our approach challenges conventional views of black holes, suggesting they may play a crucial role in the perpetuation and diversification of the cosmos.
